setup: Stand or sit tall with feet hip-width apart and your shoulders relaxed down away from your ears.
Bring one arm straight across your chest at approximately shoulder height.
steps: Place your opposite hand or forearm on the triceps of the outstretched arm, just above the elbow.
Gently pull the arm closer toward your chest until you feel a comfortable stretch along the back of the shoulder.
Hold the position steadily without bouncing.
Release slowly and repeat on the opposite arm.
instructions.breathing: Breathe smoothly and deeply throughout the hold, using each exhalation to sink gently into the stretch.
cues: Pull above the elbow, not on the joint

common_faults.fault: Shrugging the shoulder of the stretched arm upward toward the ear.
common_faults.correction: Actively depress the shoulder blade and keep the neck long before pulling the arm across.

common_faults.fault: Rotating the torso in the direction of the pull, reducing the stretch on the shoulder.
common_faults.correction: Keep your hips and chest squared straight forward throughout the stretch.

common_faults.fault: Pressing directly on the elbow joint.
common_faults.correction: Place the assisting hand on the back of the upper arm or forearm, avoiding direct pressure on the joint.

precautions: Do not force the arm past a gentle stretch; aggressive horizontal adduction can cause anterior impingement.

name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch
summary: A static upper-body stretch that elongates the posterior deltoid, rotator cuff, and upper back by pulling one arm across the chest.
